title: Basis Note of the Grain Accounting Desk: How Far Past the Fiscal-Year Close a Settlement Is Gathered Into the Year
content:
How far past the close of the fiscal year a late settlement is still gathered into the year, for the purpose of the grain volume a member earns under Membership and Patronage Equity, depends on what the member still has working on their Grain Marketing Contracts.

| What stands on the member's grain contracts | Settlements left to the new fiscal year |
| --- | --- |
| a Delayed Price Agreement with unpriced bushels still standing against it, and a grain contract standing in delivering | those recorded in the 2 months up to today; everything earlier is gathered into the year that closed |
| a grain contract standing in delivering, and no unpriced bushels standing against a Delayed Price Agreement | those recorded in the 4 months up to today |
| neither of the above | those recorded in the 5 months up to today |

**On the first line.** Both limbs must hold together: unpriced bushels must still stand against a Delayed Price Agreement on the member's Grain Marketing Contracts, and a grain contract must stand in delivering. Where both hold, only the settlements of the last 2 months are left to the new fiscal year, and everything recorded earlier is gathered into the year that closed.

**On the second line.** A grain contract stands in delivering but no unpriced bushels stand against a Delayed Price Agreement; the reach is then the 4 months up to today.

**On the third line.** Neither limb holds: there is no grain contract standing in delivering, whatever the pricing position. The reach is the 5 months up to today.

## Points of judgement on hypothetical records

| Delayed Price Agreement with unpriced bushels | A grain contract standing in delivering | Settlements left to the new year |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | yes | 2 months |
| no | yes | 4 months |
| yes | no | 5 months |
| no | no | 5 months |

The third line of the table is worth reading twice: unpriced bushels alone, with no contract standing in delivering, do not shorten the reach, because the first line requires both limbs and the second requires a contract in delivering.
